reuse.why: Every consumer (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and the schedule template) goes through one shared getOccurrenceAfterWeekendRule built on the existing weekend helper.

duplication.why: The weekend/holiday/daily rule exists once, but the candidate-window sizing heuristics (count*7, 7+2*holidays, 2+2*holidays padding) are repeated in three slightly different forms.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts with the other date helpers; the handler sits in schedules/app.ts next to get-upcoming-dates.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the weekend rule, its callers, the new handler and the holidays type.

maintainability.why: A single rule function with private helpers is easy to evolve, though the ad hoc look-ahead margins are fragile and spread across files.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter (now private); all call sites use getOccurrenceAfterWeekendRule in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts
